report.incidentSummary: At market open (09:15 IST / 03:45 UTC on 2026-10-12), stock order placement experienced a spike in failures (~19.5% error rate on order-service and ~14.3% on broker-connector) lasting until approximately 09:42 IST (04:12 UTC). The failures were caused by the upstream broker API returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests on 'POST /orders' when incoming order request volume surged to 915.6 req/s. order-service CPU spiked to 82.3% driven by the ~7x traffic burst and retries, but internal latency remained bounded (~614 ms p95) and database metrics remained healthy.
report.rootCauseStatement: The external broker API's order placement endpoint rate limits were exceeded by the market open order surge (order requests spiked from ~129 req/s to 915.6 req/s), causing broker-connector to receive HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses and order-service to fail order placements after exhausted retries.

hypotheses.cause: External broker API rate limits on order placement were exceeded by the market-open traffic surge, returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests to broker-connector and resulting in order placement failures on order-service.
hypotheses.rationale: broker-connector logs record 281 occurrences of 'POST /orders -> 429 Too Many Requests (limit req/s; retry-after s)' starting at 03:45:00Z. Breakdown by endpoint confirms rate limiting was concentrated on endpoint='orders' (peaking at 881.6/min). order-service logs confirm 231 order rejections explicitly stating 'order rejected: broker rate limit after retries'. The onset (03:45 UTC) and recovery (04:12-04:15 UTC) align exactly with the traffic surge and subsidence.

hypotheses.cause: order-service CPU saturation and compute resource starvation caused order drops and timeouts at market open.
hypotheses.rationale: While order-service CPU peaked at 82.28% and worker queue alerts fired, latency_p95_ms peaked at only 614.1 ms, far below the 3,000 ms gateway timeout. Furthermore, order-service error logs show zero timeout errors; the dominant error was explicit downstream rejection due to broker rate limits (231 errors).

hypotheses.cause: Primary database lock contention or connection pool starvation caused order-service failures.
hypotheses.rationale: database db_lock_wait_ms remained normal and flat at ~4 ms, active connections stayed steady at ~176 out of capacity, order-service db_pool_wait_ms stayed below 5 ms, and database logs showed no lock contention or deadlocks.

facts.statement: order-service error_rate surged from 0.42% at 03:40 UTC (09:10 IST) to 15.73% at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), peaking at 19.52% at 03:50 UTC, and dropped back to 0.44% by 04:15 UTC (09:45 IST).
broker-connector rate_limited_count spiked from ~0/min to 632.2/min at 03:45 UTC, peaking at 881.6/min at 04:00 UTC, subsiding to ~0/min by 04:15 UTC.
broker-connector error rate by endpoint shows rate limiting was almost entirely on endpoint 'orders' (peaking at 881.6/min), while 'quotes' and 'holdings' remained negligible (<0.6/min).
broker-connector logged 281 occurrences of 'POST /orders -> 429 Too Many Requests (limit req/s; retry-after s)' between 03:45:00Z and 04:11:57Z.
order-service logs recorded 231 instances of 'order <ref> rejected: broker rate limit (#) after # retries' between 03:45:40Z and 04:11:49Z.
order-service request rate jumped from 129.2 req/s at 03:40 UTC to 915.6 req/s at 03:45 UTC, while latency_p95_ms rose from 320.6 ms to 614.1 ms.
No deployments, configuration changes, or feature flags occurred across api-gateway, broker-connector, database, or order-service within 12 hours prior to the incident.
database db_lock_wait_ms remained steady between 3.78 ms and 4.13 ms, and active_connections remained flat at 171-180 throughout 03:15 to 05:15 UTC.

inferences.statement: The high order-service CPU utilization (82.28%) was a secondary symptom of handling a 7x surge in incoming order traffic (915.6 req/s) and executing order retries, rather than primary CPU saturation causing timeouts.
Orders failed at the user layer because broker-connector received HTTP 429 from the external broker and propagated failures back to order-service once order-service exhausted its retry budget.

assumptions.statement: The upstream broker API enforces strict transactional rate limits per second on the order placement route during market open rush.

timeline.event: Pre-market baseline: order-service request rate at 129.2 req/s, error rate at 0.42%, broker-connector rate limits at 0.4/min.
Market opens: order-service requests surge to 915.6 req/s; external broker begins returning 429 Too Many Requests on POST /orders (632.2/min); order-service error rate spikes to 15.73%.
Peak order-service error rate reaches 19.52%; broker-connector error rate peaks at 14.26%.
Rate limited requests peak at 881.6/min on broker-connector; on-call SRE reports SEV1 incident INC-5946 suspecting order-service overload.
Last 429 responses received by broker-connector (04:11:57 UTC) and last broker rate limit error logged by order-service (04:11:49 UTC).
Traffic moderates to 273.7 req/s; rate limited count returns to baseline (0/min) and error rates subside to 0.44% on order-service and 0.20% on broker-connector.

confidence.rationale: Direct and corroborating evidence from broker-connector error logs (ev_9), broker-connector endpoint-tagged rate limit metrics (ev_22), and order-service error logs (ev_18) unequivocally demonstrate that failures were caused by upstream broker 429 rate limits on order placement.

gaps.description: Specific TPS limit configured on the upstream broker account was not directly visible via internal logs/metrics.
gaps.impact: Minimal impact on root cause identification; does not prevent establishing that the quota was exceeded.

recommendedActions.action: Coordinate with the external broker provider to increase market-open TPS and concurrency limits for POST /orders.
recommendedActions.rationale: Current broker quota is insufficient for peak market open burst (>900 req/s across all users).
recommendedActions.verification: Confirm broker contract documentation and SLA guarantees for peak burst TPS.

recommendedActions.action: Implement a token-bucket rate limiter and queueing mechanism in broker-connector with jittered backoff aligned to the broker's Retry-After header.
recommendedActions.rationale: Prevents bursts from hitting the upstream broker unthrottled and avoids retry storms from order-service.
recommendedActions.verification: Load test broker-connector under simulated burst conditions to verify orders are shaped smoothly without incurring HTTP 429 rejections.

recommendedActions.action: Tune order-service autoscaling and client-facing error messaging to inform users when broker order-routing queues are full.
recommendedActions.rationale: Ensures order-service handles opening rush with lower queue wait times and gives users accurate feedback rather than generic placement errors.
recommendedActions.verification: Review order-service thread pool queue metrics and client error telemetry during subsequent market opens.

report.justification: Although the automated investigation round stopped at the deadline following task failures in round 1, the evidence ledger already contains the necessary records (ev_16, ev_17, ev_18, ev_22) that completely resolve the critic's prior objection. Specifically, ev_18 proves that order-service errors were 231 explicit rejections due to downstream broker rate limits after retries, ev_22 proves rate limiting occurred specifically on the orders endpoint, and ev_17 confirms order-service latency remained healthy at ~614 ms p95 (disproving service timeouts or resource starvation).

honesty.note: reported conclusive although the run stopped (deadline) without critic acceptance; the report gives a justification

# Investigation report: Stock orders failing at market open

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** deadline · **Confidence:** 0.95 · **Written by:** reporting agent
> Honesty check: reported conclusive although the run stopped (deadline) without critic acceptance; the report gives a justification

## Summary
At market open (09:15 IST / 03:45 UTC on 2026-10-12), stock order placement experienced a spike in failures (~19.5% error rate on order-service and ~14.3% on broker-connector) lasting until approximately 09:42 IST (04:12 UTC). The failures were caused by the upstream broker API returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests on 'POST /orders' when incoming order request volume surged to 915.6 req/s. order-service CPU spiked to 82.3% driven by the ~7x traffic burst and retries, but internal latency remained bounded (~614 ms p95) and database metrics remained healthy.

**Root cause:** The external broker API's order placement endpoint rate limits were exceeded by the market open order surge (order requests spiked from ~129 req/s to 915.6 req/s), causing broker-connector to receive HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses and order-service to fail order placements after exhausted retries.

## Hypotheses
1. **External broker API rate limits on order placement were exceeded by the market-open traffic surge, returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests to broker-connector and resulting in order placement failures on order-service.** — `broker-connector`, rate_limiting_or_quota, confidence 0.95, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_3, ev_4, ev_6, ev_9, ev_15, ev_16, ev_18, ev_20, ev_21, ev_22] · Contradicting: none
   - broker-connector logs record 281 occurrences of 'POST /orders -> 429 Too Many Requests (limit req/s; retry-after s)' starting at 03:45:00Z. Breakdown by endpoint confirms rate limiting was concentrated on endpoint='orders' (peaking at 881.6/min). order-service logs confirm 231 order rejections explicitly stating 'order rejected: broker rate limit after retries'. The onset (03:45 UTC) and recovery (04:12-04:15 UTC) align exactly with the traffic surge and subsidence.
2. **order-service CPU saturation and compute resource starvation caused order drops and timeouts at market open.** — `order-service`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.10, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_6, ev_11, ev_18, ev_19] · Contradicting: [ev_16, ev_17, ev_18]
   - While order-service CPU peaked at 82.28% and worker queue alerts fired, latency_p95_ms peaked at only 614.1 ms, far below the 3,000 ms gateway timeout. Furthermore, order-service error logs show zero timeout errors; the dominant error was explicit downstream rejection due to broker rate limits (231 errors).
3. **Primary database lock contention or connection pool starvation caused order-service failures.** — `database`, capacity_saturation, confidence 0.05, ruled_out
   - Supporting: [ev_5] · Contradicting: [ev_2, ev_7, ev_8]
   - database db_lock_wait_ms remained normal and flat at ~4 ms, active connections stayed steady at ~176 out of capacity, order-service db_pool_wait_ms stayed below 5 ms, and database logs showed no lock contention or deadlocks.

## Facts
- order-service error_rate surged from 0.42% at 03:40 UTC (09:10 IST) to 15.73% at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), peaking at 19.52% at 03:50 UTC, and dropped back to 0.44% by 04:15 UTC (09:45 IST). [ev_6, ev_21]
- broker-connector rate_limited_count spiked from ~0/min to 632.2/min at 03:45 UTC, peaking at 881.6/min at 04:00 UTC, subsiding to ~0/min by 04:15 UTC. [ev_3, ev_20]
- broker-connector error rate by endpoint shows rate limiting was almost entirely on endpoint 'orders' (peaking at 881.6/min), while 'quotes' and 'holdings' remained negligible (<0.6/min). [ev_22]
- broker-connector logged 281 occurrences of 'POST /orders -> 429 Too Many Requests (limit req/s; retry-after s)' between 03:45:00Z and 04:11:57Z. [ev_9]
- order-service logs recorded 231 instances of 'order <ref> rejected: broker rate limit (#) after # retries' between 03:45:40Z and 04:11:49Z. [ev_18]
- order-service request rate jumped from 129.2 req/s at 03:40 UTC to 915.6 req/s at 03:45 UTC, while latency_p95_ms rose from 320.6 ms to 614.1 ms. [ev_16, ev_17]
- No deployments, configuration changes, or feature flags occurred across api-gateway, broker-connector, database, or order-service within 12 hours prior to the incident. [ev_10, ev_12]
- database db_lock_wait_ms remained steady between 3.78 ms and 4.13 ms, and active_connections remained flat at 171-180 throughout 03:15 to 05:15 UTC. [ev_2, ev_7, ev_8]

## Inferences
- The high order-service CPU utilization (82.28%) was a secondary symptom of handling a 7x surge in incoming order traffic (915.6 req/s) and executing order retries, rather than primary CPU saturation causing timeouts. [ev_1, ev_16, ev_17, ev_18]
- Orders failed at the user layer because broker-connector received HTTP 429 from the external broker and propagated failures back to order-service once order-service exhausted its retry budget. [ev_4, ev_9, ev_15, ev_18, ev_22]

## Assumptions
- The upstream broker API enforces strict transactional rate limits per second on the order placement route during market open rush.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-12 09:10 IST (03:40 UTC)** Pre-market baseline: order-service request rate at 129.2 req/s, error rate at 0.42%, broker-connector rate limits at 0.4/min. [ev_3, ev_6, ev_16]
- **2026-10-12 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC)** Market opens: order-service requests surge to 915.6 req/s; external broker begins returning 429 Too Many Requests on POST /orders (632.2/min); order-service error rate spikes to 15.73%. [ev_3, ev_6, ev_9, ev_16, ev_18, ev_22]
- **2026-10-12 09:20 IST (03:50 UTC)** Peak order-service error rate reaches 19.52%; broker-connector error rate peaks at 14.26%. [ev_4, ev_6, ev_21]
- **2026-10-12 09:30 IST (04:00 UTC)** Rate limited requests peak at 881.6/min on broker-connector; on-call SRE reports SEV1 incident INC-5946 suspecting order-service overload. [ev_3, ev_20]
- **2026-10-12 09:41-09:42 IST (04:11-04:12 UTC)** Last 429 responses received by broker-connector (04:11:57 UTC) and last broker rate limit error logged by order-service (04:11:49 UTC). [ev_9, ev_18]
- **2026-10-12 09:45 IST (04:15 UTC)** Traffic moderates to 273.7 req/s; rate limited count returns to baseline (0/min) and error rates subside to 0.44% on order-service and 0.20% on broker-connector. [ev_3, ev_4, ev_6, ev_16]

## Confidence
0.95: Direct and corroborating evidence from broker-connector error logs (ev_9), broker-connector endpoint-tagged rate limit metrics (ev_22), and order-service error logs (ev_18) unequivocally demonstrate that failures were caused by upstream broker 429 rate limits on order placement.

## Gaps
- Specific TPS limit configured on the upstream broker account was not directly visible via internal logs/metrics. (impact: Minimal impact on root cause identification; does not prevent establishing that the quota was exceeded.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Coordinate with the external broker provider to increase market-open TPS and concurrency limits for POST /orders. [ev_9, ev_16, ev_18, ev_22]
  - Why: Current broker quota is insufficient for peak market open burst (>900 req/s across all users).
  - Verify: Confirm broker contract documentation and SLA guarantees for peak burst TPS.
- **[next]** Implement a token-bucket rate limiter and queueing mechanism in broker-connector with jittered backoff aligned to the broker's Retry-After header. [ev_9, ev_18]
  - Why: Prevents bursts from hitting the upstream broker unthrottled and avoids retry storms from order-service.
  - Verify: Load test broker-connector under simulated burst conditions to verify orders are shaped smoothly without incurring HTTP 429 rejections.
- **[later]** Tune order-service autoscaling and client-facing error messaging to inform users when broker order-routing queues are full. [ev_1, ev_17, ev_18]
  - Why: Ensures order-service handles opening rush with lower queue wait times and gives users accurate feedback rather than generic placement errors.
  - Verify: Review order-service thread pool queue metrics and client error telemetry during subsequent market opens.

## Justification
Although the automated investigation round stopped at the deadline following task failures in round 1, the evidence ledger already contains the necessary records (ev_16, ev_17, ev_18, ev_22) that completely resolve the critic's prior objection. Specifically, ev_18 proves that order-service errors were 231 explicit rejections due to downstream broker rate limits after retries, ev_22 proves rate limiting occurred specifically on the orders endpoint, and ev_17 confirms order-service latency remained healthy at ~614 ms p95 (disproving service timeouts or resource starvation).
